sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Chartering and Operation of Offshore Platform Support Ships

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT), as amended by Ley No. 70 de 2019 and related implementing regulations; Decreto Ejecutivo No. 265 de 2019 on the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales; Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995, as amended, on Private Interest Foundations; implementing resolutions and directives of the Registro Público de Panamá and the Unidad de Análisis Financiero.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certificate of no impediment of the corporate founder or parent entity, if any
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or commercial register in the country of incorporation of the founder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified extract of the corporate resolution of the founder authorizing the establishment of the Private Interest Foundation and appointing its representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, board of directors or equivalent governing body of the founder entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney granted by the founder and/or ultimate beneficial owners to the Panamanian resident agent and attorney-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the jurisdiction where the grantor executes the document

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and beneficial ownership/PEP declaration of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority, a registered agent, or a notary as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Vessel registration transcript or flag-state bareboat charter certificate if a vessel is to be directly or beneficially owned by the Foundation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panama Maritime Authority or the relevant flag-state maritime registry

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under Ley No. 23 de 2015 and UAF directives. The registered agent must identify the founder, council members, protector, beneficiaries and all individual or legal-entity owners holding direct or indirect control or 25% or more of the Foundation; screen continuously against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN/SSI lists, EU consolidated lists, and Panama national sanctions lists maintained by the UAF. PEP status triggers enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval. Unfavourable sanctions hits or refusal to provide UBO information must stop the incorporation engagement and may require a suspicious transaction report to the UAF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Portal en Línea del Registro Público de Panamá - Servicio de Reserva de Nombre y Edicto Electrónico (www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Private Interest Foundation name must be stated in Spanish or in any Latin-alphabet European language. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters for registry indexing. The name must contain the word 'Foundation' or 'Fundación' or a recognised abbreviation to identify the legal structure. The Registro Público applies similarity and misleading-sound rules to avoid confusion with existing entities.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Before expiration, the applicant may file an administrative extension or new reservation with the Registro Público and pay the applicable official fee. If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request (recurso de reconsideración) before the Dirección General del Registro Público within the statutory administrative-appeal period. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may pursue the administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) and ultimately judicial review before the Contencioso-Administrativo Chamber of the Corte Suprema de Justicia.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable only as a supplementary correspondence and management convenience. It cannot replace the mandatory physical registered office and resident agent in Panama required by the Private Interest Foundation Law and the AML/CFT legal framework. For an offshore supply vessel leasing operation, the Maritime Authority expects genuine operational substance and may reject a purely virtual lessor structure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 60-70% for AMP-regulated maritime activities due to vessel certification, safety and operational compliance checks; 25-35% for unannounced resident-agent and registered-office inspections under AML/CFT supervision. Unannounced inspections are legally permitted.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry name search and 30-day reservation of the Private Interest Foundation name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory tariff under Registro Público fee regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial execution of the foundation deed (acta constitutiva) and drafting of the charter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark and notarial tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the foundation deed in the Public Registry and issuance of the foundation inscription certificate
First-year resident agent and registered office physical-address fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian resident agent or registered agent firm

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT onboarding, UBO declaration, and PEP/sanctions screening fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance officer of the registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing compliance service benchmark under Ley No. 23 de 2015

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille/consular legalization, and certified translation of foreign corporate and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization unit and foreign competent authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official apostille/legalization fees and certified translation market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year annual foundation tax (franchise fee) prefunded at incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos, Ministry of Economy and Finance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory annual fiscal tariff applicable to Private Interest Foundations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Maritime licensing preliminary technical and AML review for offshore supply vessel leasing under ISIC 5222
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama Maritime Authority and external maritime counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing maritime legal benchmark and AMP pre-consultation administrative fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Régimen de las Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended; Executive Decree No. 1358 of 2013 (registration regulation); Código Fiscal arts. 694-709 (territorial source taxation); Ley No. 23 de 2015, as amended (beneficial ownership disclosure through the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Departamento de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Ancon, Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter) submitted in original notarized form and inscribed in the Foundation Registry; issuance of the Certificado de Inscripción and appointment of the registered agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum endowed patrimony of USD 10,000 (or legal equivalent) declared in the Foundation Charter pursuant to Law 25 of 1995, Article 8. The endowment may be constituted in installments or through non-cash assets; Panama law imposes no escrow deposit, no paid-up certification, and no banker's verification at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: In the Republic of Panama, on this date, the Founder declares a minimum endowment of USD 10,000 and the lawful purpose of offshore supply vessel leasing and chartering (ISIC 5222), ratifying the Foundation Charter as inscribed in the Public Registry. RESOLVED: The registered office is established at the address registered in Panama and the licensed resident agent is confirmed. RESOLVED: The Foundation Council is elected, comprising the President, Secretary, and Treasurer. RESOLVED: The Council is authorized to open maritime escrow and wire-transfer accounts, execute bareboat charter and lease agreements, appoint the AMP representative, and delegate DGI tax filings. RESOLVED: The Foundation shall operate under territorial taxation and pay annual registry fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Primer Circuito Judicial, Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Charter in Spanish including endowment, registered agent acceptance, purpose of offshore supply vessel leasing, Foundation Council members, and complementary provisions. The founder or duly authorized attorney-in-fact must appear personally before the notary with valid identification. The notary authenticates signatures and delivers the testimonio (first notarized copy) for presentation to the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or cédula of the founder
Registered agent acceptance letter from a licensed Panamanian attorney
Draft Foundation Charter in original and two copies
Identification and contact details of Foundation Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect, a diligencia aclaratoria (notarial corrective amendment) is executed and incorporated before filing; if the founder is unavailable, a notarial power of attorney must be executed in advance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Private Interest Foundation with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Departamento de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized testimonio, registered agent acceptance, and evidence of payment of the tariff through the Registry's foundation subdivision or an authorized attorney e-account. The Registry's calificación process verifies statutory form and lawful purpose, then issues the Certificado de Inscripción and records the registered agent appointment and Council members.
required_dossiers: Notarized testimonio of the Foundation Charter
Registered agent acceptance letter and copy of resident agent license
Copy of founder identification and declaration of endowment
Payment receipt for official registry tariffs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If calificación is denied, the applicant may cure noted deficiencies within ten working days by filing a notarized addendum; administrative remedies include recurso de reconsideración and recurso de apelación against the Registrar's calificación note.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer registration (NIT) with the General Directorate of Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas — SIGIT online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent accesses SIGIT, selects the Private Interest Foundation registration form, enters the inscription data, declares economic activity ISIC 5222 (chartering and operation of offshore platform support ships), and obtains the NIT certificate and aviso de inscripción. Beneficial ownership information is simultaneously declared for the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales.
required_dossiers: Certificado de inscripción from the Public Registry
Copy of the inscribed Foundation Charter
Registered agent NIT and power of representation
Foundation Council resolution approving tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIGIT validation flags data inconsistencies, the filing is corrected and resubmitted; a formal correction may be filed with DGI per Código Fiscal Article 1144, and the amended NIT certificate is reissued accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal operation notice and commercial premises license
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá — Dirección General de Rentas Municipales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the DGI NIT certificate and Registry inscription to the municipal treasury window or electronic platform, declare the business activities of ocean vessel leasing and offshore marine chartering, declare the registered office location, pay the opening fee, and obtain the Aviso de Operación to be displayed at the registered office and renewed annually.
required_dossiers: DGI NIT registration certificate
Certificado de inscripción of the Foundation
Lease agreement or right of use over the registered office
Identification of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Aviso is queried for missing municipal patent endorsement, the applicant pays the difference in the annual tasa municipal and presents a notarized solvencia municipal to finalize the issuance; address corrections are cured through the municipal rectification window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maritime operating license for offshore supply vessel chartering
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Autoridad Marítima de Panamá (AMP) — Dirección General de Marina Mercante
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for the OSV operator license (Licencia de Operador de Naves de Apoyo Marítimo), submitting corporate inscription documents, vessel particulars and flag certificates, P&I insurance evidence, and designation of a local maritime agent. The license authorizes the Foundation to charter and lease offshore support vessels to E&P contractors operating on the Panamanian continental margin and internationally.
required_dossiers: Certificado de inscripción and inscribed Foundation Charter
Vessel particulars: tonnage certificate, flag registration, ISM compliance document
Protection and Indemnity insurance certificate
Appointment of AMP licensed local maritime agent or operator
DGI NIT and municipal aviso de operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMP docket raises a technical objection, the applicant has fifteen working days to subsanar; an adverse final decision may be appealed to the AMP Board of Directors within five working days and thereafter to the maritime administrative jurisdiction before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autoridad Marítima de Panamá (AMP) — Dirección General de Marina Mercante, jointly with the Dirección General de Puertos e Industrias Marítimas Auxiliares for any shore-side staging facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Operador de Naves de Apoyo Marítimo / Permiso de Arrendamiento de Buques de Suministro Costa Afuera (Offshore Supply Vessel Operator License)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Verificación del Desempeño Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I — Aviso Ambiental / Diagnóstico Ambiental de Bajo Impacto (stationary low-impact registration applicable because the Foundation performs chartering and bareboat leasing with no fixed point source; a full Category II or III EIA is required only if the project adds shore-based repair yards, fuel storage, or base terminals).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: All chartered vessels must operate under PANAMA-ratified MARPOL Annexes I, IV, V, and VI: oily-water discharge limited to 15 ppm through approved separators, controlled sewage discharge, special-area waste handling, and compliance with the 0.5% m/m global sulfur cap. Shore-side staging facilities, if introduced, must meet DGNTI-COPANIT 47-2000 wastewater thresholds and use authorized waste reception facilities, including Panama Canal Tripartite Agreement reception arrangements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire safety inspection and certificate for the registered office and any shore staging area; Dirección General de Normas y Tecnología Industrial structural load clearance where lifting or weight-bearing equipment is staged; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) workplace registration and annual occupational safety report; vessels in operation must maintain International Safety Management (ISM) Code certification and ISPS compliance for offshore platform calls.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama; operational portal: Sistema de Facturación Electrónica and e-Tax 2.0 (https://etax.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity (including a Private Interest Foundation) must appoint a resident legal representative and register with DGI to obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC). The application is submitted via e-Tax 2.0 or in person at DGI offices, providing the foundation's registered articles, certificate of foundation, registered agent details, a local service address, and statutory declaration of economic activity. DGI issues the RUC within 5–10 business days. The RUC is required for invoicing, VAT/ITBMS registration, and customs transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a check-the-box regime; tax classification follows the statutory form. A Private Interest Foundation is a separate legal entity; if it exercises commercial activities in Panama, it elects to be taxed as a corporation under the territorial income tax rules. A PIF may also elect the Simplified Regime for Small Taxpayers if annual gross income does not exceed B/.200,000. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available; taxpayers may, however, elect to apply OECD-aligned transfer pricing documentation thresholds and, under specific conditions, enter into advance pricing agreements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) – VAT equivalent
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 annual taxable turnover (gross sales of movable goods and services; DGI Resolution No. 201-1581 of 2009, as updated by digital economy reforms)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) is phased from 2022 to 2025 for all ITBMS-registered taxpayers, including large, medium, and small taxpayers. The system requires real-time transmission of e-invoices to DGI via the 'Sistema de Facturación Electrónica' using DGI-authorized XML schemas, a digital signature certificate, and a unique successive authorization number (NIF). Invoices must carry a QR code verifying DGI clearance, and all records must be archived for six years. API integration is required for enterprise financial systems, and the framework is aligned with the Central American Digital Integration System.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Panama are subject to a 0% ITBMS rate. Services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated if the benefit is consumed outside Panama and the supplier retains evidence of the foreign recipient's country of residence. An exporter must hold a valid exporter registration with DGI, present the actual customs export evidence, and deposit export proceeds in a Panamanian banking institution to secure the 0% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Exportación – DUE, issued by Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas)
Bill of Lading (original maritime carrier document)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank verification of export payment repatriation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panamanian tax authorities may audit export transactions for substance and timing compliance. Failure to prove physical export or to repatriate proceeds within the statutory term triggers reversal of the zero-rating, additional ITBMS at 7% plus monthly interest from the invoice date, and penalties up to 200% of the tax omitted. False documentation or fraudulent export claims constitute tax evasion under Ley 8 de 2012, subject to criminal sanctions (imprisonment up to 5 years) and prohibition from future export privileges. A retrospective clawback period of 5 years applies for fraud, and 3 years for non-fraudulent procedural errors.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Republic of Panama has no de jure central bank; the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) serves as banking regulator and overseer of the national payment system. For foreign exchange and trade related transactions, the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias and the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) have ancillary oversight. The U.S. dollar is legal tender, and the National Bank of Panama (Banco Nacional de Panamá) acts as fiscal agent but does not perform monetary control functions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions. Panama operates a dollarized, open economy with no exchange controls, no restrictions on the repatriation of profits, dividends, or capital, and no mandatory Central Bank approval for cross-border transfers. Legal tender is the U.S. dollar (USD) alongside the on-par Panamanian Balboa (PAB) which exists only as coins; bank accounts are commonly maintained in USD. For a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) engaged in offshore vessel leasing to non-residents, capital and income realized outside Panama's territorial tax jurisdiction are generally free of local tax, and remittance of charter hire and sale proceeds can be effected without FX conversion or surcharge.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama does not impose any surrender requirement, mandatory conversion timeline, or retention obligation for export proceeds. A Panama-domiciled entity may retain all USD earnings in local designated accounts or offshore accounts without reference to a statutory conversion regime. For marine service exports, including offshore supply vessel charters, invoicing is typically denominated in USD, and there is no requirement to exchange through local banks or to report export proceeds beyond the standard tax and statistical filings.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD current account for charter receivables and operational disbursements)
Capital Escrow Account / Treasury Settlement Account (multi-currency USD clearing and escrow for vessel acquisition)
Operational Account (tailored trade finance for shipping and maritime services)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility. Panama’s banking law requires formal financial infrastructure licensing for money transmission and electronic payment services; an offshore digital EMI (e.g., non-Panamanian e-money institution) cannot directly provide a local account or process local ACH/SPI transfers without partnering with a licensed Panamanian bank. Cross-border EMIs, including those from the EU or the UK, may open segregated operational accounts for the PIF only if they hold a recognized license and the PIF satisfies their global KYC rules. However, many EMIs decline Panama-domiciled foundations due to non-transparent beneficial ownership perceptions; a PIF should expect elevated due diligence requiring foundation deed, current public registry certificate (where applicable), and a certified beneficial owner affidavit.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is generally mandated for all signatories and directors of a Private Interest Foundation during the initial account opening at tier-1 Panamanian banks. Remote opening is grantable in limited circumstances for existing clients of the bank or for a non-directed foundation with a professional Panamanian resident agent conducting the interview on behalf, but for the operational profile of an offshore supply vessel lessor, most compliance officers will require an in-person interview with at least one beneficial owner or the statutory director. For non-resident founders, a video-call affordability plus apostilled documentation is occasionally accepted, but root physical presence at a Panamanian notary or consular officer remains the practical norm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-transparent ownership structure of a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) with bearer shares or unclear economic interest holders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation deed and by-laws with certified Spanish translation; certificate of the Private Interest Foundation issued by the Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público); explicit name and passport copy of any council members and founder; and a sworn declaration of the final beneficial owner (with passport, residence proof, and professional reference), followed by an organizational chart identifying the natural person controlling the vessel chartering entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore maritime charter activity regarded as high-velocity cross-border cash flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copies of the underlying charter party contracts (BIMCO SUPPLYTIME or analogous) listing the foundation as lessor; invoices and corresponding payment schedule; evidence of statutory vessel registration (Panama SEGUMAR / ship registry) or a bareboat charter-in certificate; and a 12-month projected transaction ledger showing counterparty names, vessel identifiers, and expected remittance corridors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth / source of funds ambiguity for initial vessel acquisition capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements or certified net-worth statement of the beneficial owner for the prior two years; bank reference letter from the primary bank holding the original funds; legal purchase agreement and bill of sale for the offshore supply vessel; evidence of fund remittance by external wire (SWIFT MT103) corresponding to the acquisition; and a notarized declaration of lawful source of funds compatible with Panamanian anti-money laundering (Law 23 of 2015).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP (politically exposed person) exposure associated with a vessel lessee in an international oil and gas jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening report for the PIF, the vessel beneficial owner, and charter counterparties; copies of maritime insurance certificates (P&I) covering liability; a compliance manual outlining sanctions screening procedures; engagement letters from external counsel certifying no sanctioned-party nexus; and historical flag registry details for the vessel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the Private Interest Foundation’s initial equity or debt injection (typically USD for newbuild or second-hand offshore supply vessel acquisition), routing must use a United States dollar SWIFT transfer (MT103) from the founder's home country bank to a non-resident offshore USD account held by the PIF in Panama. The purpose code should be 'Trading proceeds - capital injection for offshore vessel chartering' under the IMF Balance of Payments classification; the wire must reference the PIF's unique identification (the 'PIF' Registry number) and the underlying vessel acquisition contract. To mitigate the Enhanced Due Diligence triggered by high-value first transfer, a pre-validation letter from the receiving Panamanian bank, a certificate of good standing from the Public Registry, and a copy of the signed charter/lease warrant is required. The receiving bank may impose a 5-7 business day verification period and freeze the funds until receipt of the compliance packet. Cleared or escrow settlement for the vessel purchase should use a maritime escrow service provider regulated by the SBP or an international maritime escrow arm of a tier-1 Panamanian bank to provide a compliant trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating disbursements (crew, fuel, insurance, port dues, and maintenance) are settled via SWIFT MT103 wires or S.W.I.F.T.-based ACH equivalents (for Panamanian local beneficiary accounts) from the PIF's USD operational account. For charter hire received from leasing the offshore supply vessel to an international oil operator, receipts may be routed via (i) client bank to PIF USD account using SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'rent for offshore platform support vessel', or (ii) a commercial letter of credit (LC) issued by charterer's bank. Disbursements to suppliers typically involve MT103 or higher-tier MT202 COVER for multi-bank chains; when adapting to US banks, the PIF must ensure the account name and foundation title match the Panamanian record to avoid OFAC matching errors. For vessel disbursement hubs (e.g., Houston, Aberdeen, Singapore), the PIF can receive and disburse through a Panamanian bank's correspondent account in the US or the UK, with all payments accompanied by an invoice and voyage number.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: US Dollar (USD) is the functional currency; the Balboa (PAB) is fixed at 1:1 to the USD, meaning no cross-currency hedge is required domestically.

For charter hire quoted in non-USD currencies (e.g., GBP or EUR), fully deliverable FX forwards or cross-currency swaps are permissible through licensed Panamanian banks or international brokers, provided the instrument is for hedging of actual vessel charter exposure and not speculative.

Panama-domiciled PIFs may enter into non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only via an offshore bank with a US banking presence, and such trades are generally permitted only with proof of an underlying trade payable/receivable.
Currency swaps hedged against USD for 3-12 month charters are permissible and settlement must be in USD or PAB at the same value; no Panamanian central bank authorization is required.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation Franchise Tax (Impuesto Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado / Tasa Única Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Foundation Section) and Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) collection window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During the first quarter of each calendar year, on or before 31 March; newly incorporated foundations pay the initial fee at registration and resume the first-quarter cycle the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a 10% statutory annual surcharge; after three consecutive non-payment periods the Public Registry may suspend the foundation's juridical personality and order administrative strike-off; arrears preclude issuance of the Certificado de Persona Jurídica (Good Standing) needed for vessel charter registration, offshore supply vessel mortgage recordals, and P&I club validations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Transparency Notice (Aviso de Transparencia) reconfirming Ultimate Beneficial Owner, foundation council, protector, and beneficiary data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Panama Ultimate Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, during the specific month assigned to the entity's RUC final digit; the full staggered schedule spans 1 January through 31 December of the year following the reporting period, with RUC endings 9, 0, and 1 carrying January, February, and March deadlines respectively
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of USD 50 up to USD 500 per omission; DGI may suspend the RUC and prohibit Panamanian-source invoice issuance, blocking charter-hire collections; repeated non-filing triggers cross-referral to the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) as an AML compliance red flag.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta, Form 1021) - zero-activity return for foreign-source offshore vessel chartering revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year-end, the return is due on or before 31 March of the following year (three-month statutory window); extension requests are available through the DGI digital platform only for taxpayers with pre-existing electronic filing credentials
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties under the Fiscal Code range from USD 50 to USD 5,000, plus a monthly 10% late interest rate on any determined tax; persistent non-filing triggers RUC suspension, preventing vessel lease invoicing through Panamanian banks and customs clearances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statement Registration (Registro de Estados Financieros) - required only where Law 52 of 2016 thresholds are exceeded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Foundation and Mercantile Sections online filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the fiscal year-end (on or before 30 April for a 31 December year-end), unless the foundation qualifies for the passive-activity exemption under Law 52 of 2016 and Executive Decree 511 of 2021
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Public Registry will reject or freeze subsequent inscriptions, including foundation council changes, protector appointments, and preferred mortgage recordals over offshore supply vessels, until statements are regularized; fines up to USD 5,000 may be imposed for untimely or false registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent external audit by a Panamanian licensed CPA is compulsory when gross annual income exceeds USD 3,000,000 or total assets exceed USD 3,000,000 (Law 52 of 2016 and Executive Decree 511 of 2021); entities with gross annual income between USD 1,000,000 and USD 3,000,000 may file unaudited statements. A Private Interest Foundation earning only foreign-source charter revenue outside Panama with no Panama-situs commercial activities remains outside the compulsory audit net.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama (Law 27 of 2005) for all reporting legal entities; simplified Panamanian GAAP is acceptable for small and medium entities below the Law 52 of 2016 audit thresholds; passive foundations may maintain internal cash-basis accounting records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The foundation council or registered agent must submit the annual Aviso de Transparencia through the DGI portal, confirming the founder, foundation council members, protector (if appointed), and beneficiaries, including citizenship and address of each ultimate beneficial owner. Although a PIF has no share capital, any transfer of the founder's patrimonial interest, substitution of beneficiaries, or council membership change must first be formalized by a notarized foundation amendment registered in the Public Registry and then reconciled with the annual transparency notice; the DGI flags foundations where the Foundation Charter does not match the annual UBO confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) and testamentary provisions as registered in the Public Registry of Panama
Register of Foundation Council Members (consejo fundacional) recording current appointments, resignations, and delegated powers
Register of Beneficiaries and Protector designations with asset distribution rules
Minute Book recording annual foundation council resolutions, including approvals of offshore supply vessel charter-party agreements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 850 - USD 2,500 per annum for a Panama-licensed registered agent and resident representative, typically including Aviso de Transparencia preparation, annual fee processing, and Good Standing certificate handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 7,500 for a certified Panamanian audit engagement; not incurred while the foundation remains a passive foreign-charter vehicle below the Law 52 of 2016 audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on net Panamanian-source income; non-resident PIF with wholly foreign-source charter revenue is exempt under territoriality principle
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective tax on eligible foreign-source shipping income; statutory neutrality for private interest foundation holding assets outside Panama; no gross charter tax on international offshore vessel operations

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 300 (Declaración de Renta) filed through DGI Tax e-filing system (T@x); supplementary transfer pricing forms, where applicable, via Form 2188
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months following FYE; fiscal year defaults to calendar year unless prior authorization; filing extension available until 5th month upon formal request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from Panamanian sources and from worldwide activities attributable to Panama permanent establishment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For foreign‑source charter of offshore support vessels operated entirely outside Panama, report 0; attach descriptive memorandum of route operations and vessel location logs
Report all charter hire, demurrage, and bareboat fees received from bona fide international shipping clients; supporting invoices and bank statements required

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs and deductions attributable to Panamanian-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct direct operational expenses only if income is Panamanian-source; otherwise leave blank to preserve tax-exempt foreign status
For zero Panamanian-source activity, enter 0.00 and file declaration for bankability and compliance proof

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at 25% statutory rate, reduced by unique tax credits and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute 25% on any Panama-source net income; PIF with foreign source only shows USD 0.00 liability

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: USD 10 minimum, up to 10% of tax due; monthly surcharge of 1% of unpaid tax for first 12 months; interest at prime rate + 3%; administrative closure of tax ID and blocking of municipal permits; criminal sanctions for intentional failure to file.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed from Panamanian-source net profits; no withholding on distributions from foreign-source funds held by PIF
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama maintains a limited double taxation agreement network; relief requires filing Form 315 with DGI, attaching tax residency certificate (TRC) from counterparty jurisdiction, legalized or apostilled, with Spanish translation, and obtaining DGI clearance before reduced rate is applied; in absence of treaty, statutory 10% applies
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties paid to non-residents: 12.5%; statutory WHT on interest paid to non-residents: 10% (6% if from certified bank credit); treaty rates may be reduced to 0–5% for interest and 0–10% for royalties depending on counterparty DTA and eligible beneficiary conditions

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD: annual gross income of consolidated group exceeding USD 2,000,000 or aggregate related-party transactions exceeding USD 500,000 triggers contemporaneous Local File and Master File requirement in Panamanian pesos (US dollar equivalent)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) applicable since 2021 to Panamanian-licensed entities engaged in relevant activities; offshore supply vessel chartering is a relevant activity requiring: physical office in Panama, presence of officers and employees, adequate expenditure from Panama, and core income-generating activities carried out locally; PIF sheltered from registration but economically active maritime operators must file annual substance declaration and maintain constitutional and operational records proving nexus

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately mischaracterizing Panamanian-source revenue as foreign-source to exploit territorial exemption; fabricating vessel route logs; false statement in Form 300
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of up to 200% of evaded tax; monetary fine USD 50,000 per violation; cancellation of operating license; criminal imprisonment up to 6 years for aggravated evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, foundation council, and beneficial owners are jointly and severally liable for restitution; travel bans and asset freezing; disqualification from holding directorship in Panama; criminal prosecution may pierce PIF veil where foundation is used as a sham

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Private Interest Foundation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Utilizing PIF without economic substance to channel charter revenue and avoid ESR reporting; nominee officers without trading activity; soliciting false tax residency certificates
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foundation struck from Registry; registration voided; fines up to USD 100,000; denial of tax-protected status retroactively making all worldwide income taxable at 25% plus penalties; potential freeze of bank accounts and assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Founders and council members can be personally taxed on undistributed foundation profits under an administrative recharacterization; criminal liability for money laundering; removal and compensation orders; inability to leave Panama until tax liability satisfied

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Chartering vessel to a sanctioned state or entity; failing suspicious transaction report from payment rails (SWIFT wire / escrow maritime); understating beneficial ownership; handling shell-company nominees in vessel operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama AML penalties reach USD 1,000,000 and confiscation of the vessel and charter proceeds; refusal of registry renewal; extradition risk under international maritime law; vessel bonding and arrest; criminal sanction for economic-terrorist links up to 15 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and bearer-share principals subject to arrest, extradition, and 10-year prison term; civil liability for proceeds and damages; directors' personal assets attachable where vessel is arrested; statutory disqualification from operational duties and forced resignations within 30 days
